title: Are Inflation Expectations Currently Well Anchored? - San Francisco Fed
gist: SF Fed researchers estimate how long-run breakeven inflation reacts to FOMC surprises: -0.34 over 1999-2026, troughing near -0.89 in 2018, but near zero by June 2026 (five-year window -0.23, -0.08 with press conferences). They conclude expectations are increasingly well anchored, leaving the Fed room to tolerate temporary supply-shock inflation such as higher oil prices.

insights.claim: The SF Fed gauges the strength of the Fed's nominal anchor by how much long-run market inflation expectations respond to monetary policy surprises; a value near zero means a strong, credible anchor.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Gives a market-based, high-frequency read on Fed credibility.
insights.quote: A value of this sensitivity measure close to zero indicates a strong credible anchor

insights.claim: A significantly negative sensitivity means unexpected policy moves make markets revise their view of the Fed's commitment to its inflation goal, signaling a weaker anchor.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Negative readings flag credibility uncertainty that can amplify policy surprises.
insights.locator: By contrast, a significantly negative value

insights.claim: The measure is built from one-day changes in 5-year 5-year-forward breakeven inflation (Treasuries minus TIPS) around FOMC announcements, regressed on policy surprises from federal funds contracts spanning one month to one year.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Method is replicable from public market data.
insights.locator: Estimating perceptions of central bank credibility

insights.claim: Policy surprises are measured in a 30-minute window around the FOMC statement and a 100-minute window that also covers the press conference; 1999-2026 FOMC events are used, excluding July 2008-June 2009 for TIPS market dysfunction.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Method choices matter: the window changes the conclusion about anchoring.
insights.locator: We compute the monetary policy surprise

insights.claim: Over the full 1999-2026 sample the sensitivity measure is -0.34 and statistically significant, implying the nominal anchor may not always have been fully credible.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Long-run history shows only partial credibility.
insights.quote: Estimates for the entire 1999–2026 sample yield a sensitivity measure of –0.34.

insights.claim: A 1 percentage point unexpected tightening lowered long-run inflation expectations by roughly 0.34 percentage point, as markets raised the odds of a strongly inflation-averse Fed.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Tightening surprises lower, not raise, long-run breakevens when credibility is imperfect.

insights.claim: The most negative readings came in 2018-2020, with a five-year-window trough of -0.89 in 2018 and a 10-year-window trough of -0.81 in 2019, showing expectations risked becoming unanchored just before the pandemic.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Pre-pandemic anchor was at its weakest, a benchmark for downside risk.

insights.claim: The authors attribute the 2018-2020 weakness to persistently below-target realized inflation, which likely lowered long-run expectations.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Undershooting inflation, not overshooting, eroded the anchor.

insights.claim: Estimates began rising toward zero in 2020, likely reflecting the August 2020 adoption of average inflation targeting and the March 2022 start of the post-pandemic tightening cycle.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Both tolerance for temporary overshoots and a credible tightening reinforced the anchor.
insights.locator: The estimates for both rolling windows

insights.claim: In June 2026 the five-year rolling estimate is -0.23 and statistically indistinguishable from zero, while the 10-year estimate is -0.32, still significant but well up from its 2019 trough.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Most recent read is consistent with well-anchored expectations.

insights.claim: Adding the press conference in a 100-minute window moves the full-sample estimate from -0.34 to -0.29 and the June 2026 five-year estimate from -0.23 to -0.08 and 10-year from -0.32 to -0.22 (now insignificant).
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Communication is a meaningful source of credibility.

insights.claim: The Chair's verbal communication in recent years appears to have reinforced the credibility of the Fed's nominal anchor.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Press conferences are a policy tool for anchoring expectations.

insights.claim: Short and long rolling windows trade off responsiveness against precision: five-year detects regime shifts faster, 10-year has more events and less noise.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Read the two estimates together; the 10-year one lags regime changes.
insights.locator: The two windows reflect a tradeoff

insights.claim: Supply shocks such as bottlenecks, tariffs and rising energy prices push activity and inflation in opposite directions, forcing central banks to choose between tightening and tolerating higher inflation.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Defines the trade-off now facing the FOMC.

insights.claim: A muted policy response to supply shocks is viable only if inflation expectations are well anchored at target.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim

insights.claim: With the anchor strengthening, the FOMC may have room for a more measured approach to supply shocks such as the recent oil price increase, tolerating temporary above-target inflation.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Supports a less hawkish reaction to oil-driven inflation; a dovish-leaning signal for rates.
insights.quote: it may be feasible for the Fed to tolerate temporary above-target inflation while expectations remain well anchored

insights.claim: Even the significant 10-year estimate and the -0.34 full-sample figure suggest the anchor is not perfectly firm, so the conclusion rests on trend and recent five-year evidence rather than a settled level.
insights.speaker: Taerin Kim
insights.so_what: Residual significance in some specifications is a caveat to complacency about expectations.
